answer: Collateralized vouching resists Sybil attacks by confining unverified agents to an isolated cold-start tundra until trusted peers bond capital behind their keys. When a vouched identity commits equivocation, a slashing ripple propagates backward to penalize every upstream sponsor. Attackers incur the verifiable cost of locking slashable stake or forfeiting an aged reputation relic per identity. However, colluding cartels can still cross-vouch within closed subgraphs.
